title: Atlantic Council Convenes 2026 Iraq Dialogue in Washington on Economic Reform and Stability
detail: The Atlantic Council's Iraq Initiative convened the 2026 Iraq Dialogue in Washington, D.C. on May 13, bringing together senior Iraqi officials, US policymakers, private-sector energy executives, and regional experts. The conference focused on three themes: Iraq's economic diversification challenge amid the ongoing Hormuz crisis, the prospects for the incoming Zaidi government's reform agenda, and the security situation as the US withdrawal timeline approached September 2026. US State Department officials privately encouraged Iraqi counterparts to push Zaidi toward appointing a technocratic interior minister outside the PMF orbit. KRG representatives raised the issue of unpaid civil servant salaries and Article 140's implementation before a Kurdish audience that included diaspora investment community members. The dialogue occurred one day before parliament's scheduled confidence vote on Zaidi's partial cabinet.

title: Analysis: Iraq Oil Shipments Through Hormuz Unlikely to Recover Until Late 2026 Despite Ceasefire
detail: An Eurasia Review analysis published May 13 concluded that, despite Iran declaring the Strait of Hormuz nominally open in April following the US-Iran ceasefire, ship traffic remained far below pre-war levels through mid-May 2026. Iraq held approximately 17 million barrels in onshore storage and an estimated 20+ million barrels in floating Gulf storage awaiting viable transit. Insurance premiums for tankers transiting the Strait remained at 4-5 times pre-crisis rates as underwriters cited continuing risk from Iranian naval presence and unresolved maritime security protocols. The analysis concluded full Iraqi oil export recovery was not expected until late 2026, and that the government's $74 billion 2026 federal budget was severely underfunded due to the oil revenue shortfall. Separately, analysts noted that Iran continued to collect 'passage fees' of $1–2 million per vessel, effectively turning the Strait into a toll road.
